archetype.name: Pocket Passer (aggressive downfield)
archetype.definition: A rhythm thrower from the pocket who does his real damage on throws of 10 or more air yards. This year he is challenging tighter windows than at any point in his career and still avoiding mistakes.

report.headline: Aggressive and efficient downfield, but Noel's loss tests a still-uneven offense
report.take:
Stroud's 2026 has two halves. The first is a quarterback who has changed how he plays. His aggressiveness (throws into tight windows) is 19.84%, up 7 points on last season and well above anything in his career. Yet his bad-throw rate fell 3.4 points and he has thrown 1 interception in 247 attempts. Throwing into more traffic while missing less is the profile of a passer whose processing and placement have improved, not one who got lucky. His CPOE (completion percentage over expected) of 3.19 is 3.3 points above the league average, and he has never posted a CPOE like that in a full season.

The value sits downfield. Throws under 10 air yards added 15.4 EPA (expected points added) across 150 attempts. Throws of 10-plus added 43.6 across 93. Deep balls produce 0.537 EPA a play, intermediate throws 0.425, and the middle of the field 0.433. The drag on the offense is everything around those throws. Screens and other passes behind the line have cost 12.4 EPA. The run game ranks 25th in rushing EPA, which leaves him facing third downs at an average of 8.5 yards to go. There he is sacked often (8 of his 15 sacks) and the offense converts only 32.8%. The 2-5 record says more about those drives and a defense that allows the most explosive passes in the league than about him.

The arc since Week 3 is clearly upward. Over his last five games his EPA per dropback is 0.223, against 0.119 for the season. That would sit among the better starters, and it came with fewer sacks. The ugly early numbers trace to specific games. Week 1 brought two lost fumbles. Week 2 was a 55-attempt chase in which he threw for 353 yards and still posted negative EPA. Week 7 against the Giants was a genuine step back: 153 yards and a -9.1 CPOE. So the improvement is real, but it isn't yet steady from game to game.

The complication is personnel. Jaylin Noel, his most efficient target at 0.804 EPA per target, is done for the season after toe surgery. Nico Collins is still the engine, with 20.1 EPA on 35 targets. But Xavier Hutchinson has already drawn 40 targets at slightly negative value, and some of Noel's snaps will flow toward him. How well Stroud keeps the downfield efficiency without Noel decides whether this is a top-12 passing season or a high-volume, middling one.

strengths.title: Downfield accuracy in tighter windows
strengths.body: His deep and intermediate throws carry the offense: 0.537 EPA on deep attempts and 43.6 total EPA on throws of 10-plus air yards. He is getting there while throwing into tight windows more often than ever, with the bad-throw rate falling at the same time. That combination points to real growth rather than variance. The 36 deep attempts are a modest sample, but the career-high aggressiveness is a stable trait to build on.

strengths.title: Ball security through the air
strengths.body: An interception rate of 0.4%, seventh-best among 47 qualifiers, with only one turnover-worthy pick charted. That is a sharp break from 12 interceptions in 2024 and 8 in 2025. Some regression is coming, because no one sustains a rate this low while throwing this aggressively. Still, the lower bad-throw rate says he will stay comfortably better than league average.

strengths.title: Efficiency surge since Week 3
strengths.body: His EPA per dropback over the last five games is 0.223, roughly doubling his season mark, with a 5.5 CPOE. That stretch included a big game against Jacksonville's third-ranked defense, so it isn't purely schedule. The clean pockets in Weeks 5 and 6 helped, which is the part to watch.

concerns.title: Losing Noel, inheriting more Hutchinson
concerns.body: Noel added 18.5 EPA on just 23 targets and is out for the year. Hutchinson has turned 40 targets into negative value. Unless Kayshon Boutte (0.406 per target) absorbs most of that role, Stroud's per-dropback efficiency will lose some of its explosive edge. This is the most concrete threat to the recent surge.

concerns.title: Long third downs and sacks
concerns.body: Third downs average 8.5 yards to go and produce negative EPA, with 8 of his 15 sacks. That is largely a product of a run game ranked 25th in EPA. It is less a pocket problem, though his pressure-to-sack rate of 29.4% is worse than last season's career-best mark. With David Montgomery questionable, the early-down support may not get better soon.

concerns.title: Screen and behind-LOS game is a leak
concerns.body: Passes behind the line have a 22% success rate and have cost 12.4 EPA. That is scheme and blocking more than the quarterback, and it wipes out a large chunk of what his short game adds. It is fixable by design, but it hasn't been fixed through seven games.

trend.note: Negative or flat EPA in three of the first four games gave way to three straight strong outings in Weeks 4-6. Week 7 against the Giants was a reminder that the floor is still low. The five-game efficiency is well above the season line, and he comes off the bye.

nextGame.headline: Stingy Chargers pass defense, missing its best safety and several corners
nextGame.body:
On paper the Chargers defend quarterbacks well. They rank 9th in pass EPA allowed and hold quarterbacks to 217.7 yards a game, 4th-fewest, and they have held opposing WR1s 4.5 PPR points under their averages. Their soft spot is exactly Stroud's best area. They rank 25th in deep EPA allowed and 31st against WR2s. The game script also points to modest volume. Houston is a 4.5-point favorite (-198 on the moneyline) with a 40.5 total, facing the league's worst offense by EPA. Even so, offenses lean slightly more toward the run against this defense than they normally would. Expect efficient but not high-volume passing, with fewer of the trailing-script attempts that inflated Week 2.

Availability tilts the matchup toward Houston's passing game. Derwin James, a 94%-snap safety, is on injured reserve. Cornerbacks Donte Jackson, Deane Leonard and Rodney Shelley are all out, which thins the depth the Chargers would use in sub-packages. Linebacker Denzel Perryman may return. On Houston's side, Noel is gone for the season, and Montgomery's groin leaves the run game, already weak, possibly thinner. That could put more long-yardage downs on Stroud's plate.

keyMatchups.title: Deep shots against a depleted back end
keyMatchups.body: Stroud's deep passing produces 0.537 EPA a play, and the Chargers rank 25th in deep EPA allowed even before losing James. If the safety replacement struggles in deep coverage, this is where Stroud's ceiling game comes from. The sample on both sides is small enough that it's an angle, not a lock.

keyMatchups.title: Collins versus a WR1-stingy defense
keyMatchups.body: Opposing top receivers have finished well under their averages against the Chargers. Collins carries the passing game at 0.574 EPA per target. If the Chargers tilt coverage his way, Stroud's efficiency depends on Boutte or Hutchinson winning the WR2 role the Chargers have struggled to contain.

keyMatchups.title: Low-total, lead-protection script
keyMatchups.body: Los Angeles ranks last in offensive EPA, so Houston may play from ahead. When Stroud has led by nine-plus, his efficiency has been strong, but the volume dries up. That caps yardage more than it caps efficiency.

nextGame.watch: Who runs the routes Noel used to run, and whether Stroud keeps hunting the deep middle against a secondary without Derwin James.

restOfSeason.body:
The core of this season looks durable. He is throwing into tighter windows with fewer bad throws, a real change from his 2024-25 form rather than a hot streak. His downfield efficiency should keep him among the better passers by EPA per dropback. Two things will slide back. A 0.4% interception rate won't hold at this aggressiveness, so expect a few more picks. And the deep-ball EPA, built on 36 attempts, will likely drift down, especially without Noel's big plays. The red-zone touchdown production is decent but comes with flat EPA, so touchdown volume depends on how often the offense gets there, and a weak run game limits that.

Volume is the swing. His 266.7 yards a game was padded by early losses and a 55-attempt game. As Houston plays closer or leading games, his per-game yardage has drifted down even as efficiency rose. I'd expect roughly 230-265 passing yards a game with 1.4-1.9 touchdowns, and fantasy production around 16-19.5 PPR points. The low end comes if Hutchinson soaks up Noel's targets, the high end if Boutte steps in and the line keeps third-down sacks in check.
swingFactors: Who replaces Jaylin Noel's snaps and targets
Whether game scripts keep his attempts down

confidence.note: Seven games with a clear improvement trend, but the deep-ball sample is small and a key target was just lost.
